About this study guide

This tool supports three ways to practice: Full Quiz (a randomly sampled 50-question test proportional to system size, similar in spirit to a real written exam), Sequential Review (every question, in ground-school order, front to back), and Study by System (drill one system's question bank directly). Progress and completion are tracked separately for each.

How “Proficient” is determined

Each system tile can show a “Proficient” badge once you've made sufficient attempts in that system to assess proficiency. It's a rolling calculation, recalculating fresh each time you study that system — reflecting where you stand right now, not where you stood months ago.

A few design choices behind this, briefly:

  • Why recent attempts, not a lifetime average. Rolling, recent-performance criteria are standard practice in adaptive learning systems, used at scale by platforms like ASSISTments and Khan Academy (Pelánek & Řihák, 2017).
  • Why no extra credit for a fast correct answer. A first-attempt correct answer isn't necessarily a clean read on knowledge — multiple-choice items can be answered correctly through elimination or item-writing cues rather than actual mastery, an effect the research literature calls “test-wiseness” (Smith, 1982; Downing, 2002). Every correct answer counts the same, regardless of which attempt it took.
  • Why the badge fades with inactivity. Proficiency measured once doesn't stay true forever. This mirrors the shift aviation training itself has made away from hours-based training toward proficiency-based training, under programs like the FAA's Advanced Qualification Program (AQP) and ICAO/IATA Competency-Based Training and Assessment (CBTA) — an idea that traces back to Bloom's mastery learning model (1968).

This is a study aid, not a certifying instrument. “Proficient” means your recent performance on this system meets a defined bar — it's a prompt to keep practicing where it's absent, not a substitute for instructor evaluation or an actual checkride.

Functional Checks
Interactive Procedural Trainers — practice anytime, not scored
Fuel System Functional Check
Step 1 of 2 — press the correct switch on the synoptic
How This Check Works
  • Press the switch or valve on the synoptic for the current step. If it's correct, it moves and the check advances.
  • A wrong press does nothing at first — after 3 wrong tries, the correct control lights up for you.
  • Valves take a couple seconds to move; pump switches react instantly.
  • This is a practice trainer — nothing here is scored.
Buttons
  • Undo Last Step — backs up one step so you can redo it, without resetting the whole check.
  • Reset Check — starts the entire check over from Step 1.
  • ← Home (top left) — leaves this check and returns to the main menu. Your progress here isn't saved.
Baseline: APU running on Left Main pump. Begin the check.
Standby Rudder Functional Check
Press the STBY RUD switch to see its effect on the hydraulic system
How This Check Works
  • This synoptic shows a dual hydraulic system failure in flight — both EDPs are down.
  • Press the STBY RUD switch on the synoptic to turn it ON. The AUX pump starts, the directional valve rotates, and pressure is routed to YD1 and the rudder.
  • Press it again to turn it back OFF — the AUX pump returns to standby and the YD1 feed is removed.
  • This is a practice trainer — nothing here is scored.
Buttons
  • ← Home (top left) — leaves this check and returns to the main menu.
